6 distinct values in 10 sample rows suggests aggregation is meaningful

measures.name: total_opportunity_value
measures.description: Sum of deal amounts across all sales opportunities.
measures.rationale: Opportunity amount represents potential deal value in the sales pipeline.
evidence: sales_opportunities.amount samples: Decimal('500000.00'), Decimal('50000.00'), Decimal('25000.00')
Column is nullable (1 NULL in sample) indicating not all opportunities have amounts assigned
caveats: Some opportunities may not have amounts populated yet

measures.name: total_closed_won_value
measures.description: Sum of deal amounts for opportunities that have been won.
measures.rationale: Filtering opportunities to Closed Won stage gives actual revenue from sales.
evidence: sales_opportunities.stage samples include 'Closed Won'
sales_opportunities.stage has 5 distinct values in sample

measures.name: arr_committed_sales
measures.description: Annual recurring revenue as recorded in sales opportunities.
measures.rationale: The arr_committed column appears to represent annualized recurring revenue from deals.
evidence: sales_opportunities.arr_committed samples: Decimal('5883566.74'), Decimal('684699.08'), Decimal('250000.00')
7 distinct values in 10 sample rows, with 1 NULL
caveats: ARR values appear inconsistent with deal amounts — e.g., $500k deal has $5.9M ARR, suggesting possible data quality issues

measures.name: arr_implied_from_contract
measures.description: Annual recurring revenue calculated by annualizing deal amount based on contract length.
measures.sql_expression: SUM(CASE WHEN contract_months > 0 THEN (amount * 12.0 / contract_months) ELSE 0 END)
measures.rationale: ARR can be derived by converting deal amount to annual equivalent based on contract term.
evidence: sales_opportunities.amount and contract_months are both present
contract_months samples: 1, 1, 36, 24, 24 — showing varying contract lengths
caveats: This is a derived calculation and may not match how the business defines ARR; requires validation

measures.name: forecasted_revenue
measures.description: Sum of revenue forecasted for future periods.
measures.rationale: Forecasted amount represents expected future revenue by month and segment.

All 10 sample values are distinct, suggesting granular forecasts

data_quality_flags.title: Invoice tax calculation does not match formula
data_quality_flags.description: Tax amounts do not equal subtotal × consistent tax rate, suggesting data quality issues or varying tax rates not captured.
data_quality_flags.rationale: Sample data shows inconsistent tax rates that violate expected formula total = subtotal + tax.
evidence: Sample 1: subtotal 75000.00 + tax 6000.00 = 81000.00 (8% tax rate)
Sample 2: subtotal 252000.00 + tax 20160.00 = 272160.00 (8% tax rate)
Sample 3: subtotal 50000.00 + tax 4000.00 = 54000.00 (8% tax rate)
Tax rate appears consistent at ~8% but this should be validated across full dataset

data_quality_flags.title: ARR values inconsistent with deal amounts
data_quality_flags.description: ARR committed values are disproportionately large compared to opportunity amounts, suggesting calculation errors or misunderstanding of the metric.
data_quality_flags.rationale: ARR should represent annualized revenue but sample values show ARR exceeding total deal value by 10x or more.
evidence: Opportunity with amount $500,000 and contract 1 month has ARR $5,883,566.74 (11.7x the deal)
Opportunity with amount $50,000 and contract 1 month has ARR $684,699.08 (13.7x the deal)
Opportunity with amount $500,000 and contract 24 months has ARR $250,000.00 (reasonable annualization)
Inconsistent calculation methodology across opportunities

data_quality_flags.title: LTV estimates extremely large relative to forecasted amounts
data_quality_flags.description: Lifetime value estimates are 100-200x larger than monthly forecasted amounts, suggesting possible calculation error or unrealistic assumptions.
data_quality_flags.rationale: LTV should be a multiple of monthly/annual revenue but observed ratios seem implausibly high.
evidence: Forecast $49,421.60 with LTV $3,953,728.00 (80x monthly forecast)
Forecast $337,210.86 with LTV $80,930,606.40 (240x monthly forecast)
Forecast $56,179.75 with LTV $4,494,380.00 (80x monthly forecast)
Ratios vary widely and appear inconsistent with typical LTV:revenue multiples

data_quality_flags.title: High NULL rate in opportunity ARR field
data_quality_flags.description: ARR committed field has NULL values limiting revenue analysis completeness.
data_quality_flags.rationale: Critical revenue metric should be populated for all opportunities to enable accurate pipeline analysis.
evidence: 1 NULL value observed in 10 sample rows (10% NULL rate in sample)
Missing ARR prevents accurate revenue forecasting from pipeline

data_quality_flags.title: Customer name inconsistencies across systems
data_quality_flags.description: Same customers appear with different name formats in invoices vs opportunities, requiring fuzzy matching.
data_quality_flags.rationale: Inconsistent naming prevents straightforward joins and may cause under-counting in customer analysis.
evidence: Cyberdyne appears as 'Cyberdyne Sys' in invoices and 'Cyberdyne Systems' in opportunities
Invoices use abbreviated forms: 'Wayne Ent', 'Acme Corp.' while opportunities use full names
No standardized customer master data or ID field present

data_quality_flags.title: All sampled invoices show Paid status
data_quality_flags.description: Despite 3 distinct status values existing, all 10 samples show Paid status, limiting visibility into current receivables.
data_quality_flags.rationale: Sample may not be representative of full dataset distribution; other statuses exist but weren't sampled.
evidence: invoices.status has 3 distinct values but all 10 samples are 'Paid'
Cannot determine what other status values exist without querying full dataset

data_quality_flags.title: All sampled bank transactions are ACH type
data_quality_flags.description: Despite 2 distinct transaction types existing, all 10 samples show ACH, limiting visibility into payment method diversity.
data_quality_flags.rationale: Sample may not be representative; other payment types exist but weren't sampled.
evidence: bank_transactions.type has 2 distinct values but all 10 samples are 'ACH'
Cannot determine what the second transaction type is without additional data

data_quality_flags.title: Sales rep identifier formats differ across tables
data_quality_flags.description: Opportunities use email addresses while forecasts use usernames, making it difficult to link sales rep performance.
data_quality_flags.rationale: Inconsistent identifiers prevent straightforward analysis of individual sales rep performance vs forecast.
evidence: sales_opportunities.owner_email: 'bob.martinez@example.com', 'alice.chen@example.com'
revenue_forecast.owner: 'grace.li', 'frank.singh', 'emma.park'
No overlapping names between the two samples, unclear if same people

data_quality_flags.title: Nullable fields in core business metrics
data_quality_flags.description: Several important fields allow NULLs which may complicate aggregations and reporting.
data_quality_flags.rationale: NULLs in business-critical fields require careful handling in calculations and reporting.
evidence: Multiple core metrics allow NULL: opportunity amount, ARR, close date, contract months, invoice due date
This may indicate data quality issues or legitimate business cases (e.g., opportunities without amounts yet)
